items.title: Deliverance is key to a new beginning, by Funmi Komolafe
items.description: Beloved, we thank God for life as we progress in the month of a new beginning. A new beginning means an end to old challenges, it is the time when we sing a new song, it could also mean the time that people call one by a new name. New signifies a departure from the old. Either in the physical or spiritual world, new beginning calls for celebration. It ushers in relief, it ushers in joy that we all cherish. Brethren, there are several routes to a new beginning. Some, within our control, others beyond our control. However, a combination of both the physical and the spiritual often lead to a new beginning. I’ll start by sharing the testimony of a medical doctor known for dismissing spiritual healings. He believes healing began and ended in the Bible days. Then suddenly his young daughter became ill. He put his expertise to work but his daughter was not healed, she continued to experience a raise in temperature. Then his mother told him to take the child to the church. He agreed and they went to Mountain of Fire and Miracle Ministries ( MFM) where the grandmother worships. To the glory of God after series of prayers, the little girl’s temperature became normal and she got healed. You could see that the devil and his agents tormented the doctor as if to tell him that his knowledge of medical science isn’t enough to heal his daughter. The doctor said, he had tried everything within his knowledge but his daughter’s temperature remained high. To the glory of God, after prayers of a few hours, her temperature crashed and she was healed. The human action there is that of the grandmother’s faith that believed the girl was attacked by spiritual forces and that the power of God would defeat them. The second was the agreement to go to the church. What if the parents prevented her from going to the church.? Her family took physical steps and met with the power of God that gave her the healing miracle. Beloved, see what the combination of physical steps and the spiritual action produced. For the first time, I saw her father, a medical doctor who previously didn’t believe that the forces of darkness could manipulate a person’s health or situation testify to the power of God. The point here is that the power of God delivered the young girl from the forces of darkness. So what is that issue that has held you down or stood as an obstacle to your prayers that has prevented you from getting your prayers answered.? Let’s consider an account in 2nd Kings 4 vs. 1-7 ( KJV). It tells the story of one of the wife of a prophet, whose husband had died and was heavily indebted and the creditors had come to take away her two sons to be “ bondmen”. Verses 2- 7 : “ And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil. Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels ; borrow not a few. And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels , and thou shalt set aside that which is full. So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out. And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her , There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed. Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest”. The first physical action the widow took here was to cry to Elisha for help. Her faith made her cry to the man of God. She knew that God is the only one that could reverse her financial situation. For you, whom do you cry to? Friends, relations or in-laws? Take a cue from the widow, take your case to God. You would say she went to Elisha. Yes but she must have heard testimonies of miracles that Elisha performed. These must have made her to approach him. Then she obeyed his instruction to go and borrow vessels. The act of going from house to house to borrow vessels was another action. She went to her neighbours and got vessels. What if she wasn’t in good terms with her neighbours? A lesson here is that we should never allow whatever challenge we have to affect our relationship with others. She wouldn’t have been able to go to them if she didn’t have a good relationship with her neighbours but thank God she was in good terms with her neighbours. The word that Elisha spoke delivered her from indebtedness. She got delivered and had a new beginning of a debt free life. Indeed she had an overflow of financial blessings such that she was no longer called a debtor. God put to shame those that wanted to put her sons into slavery because of the debt she owed. By the grace of God, if your detractors continue to mock you, God would show up with a miracle for you when they least expect in Jesus name. The widow here got a new beginning of financial independence. The miracle opened her mouth for a new song. Brethren, there are conditions for one to be delivered. I make reference to a previous sermon of our father in the Lord, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God. He once said, the person that is in bondage must be willing to be delivered. Have you been a victim of spiritual husband that has sex with a man in the dream? Unless, such a person is delivered, to achieve pregnancy would be difficult. A woman that finds herself in that position must go to a true man or woman of God for deliverance. Once Jesus steps in and she is delivered, the long awaited baby or babies would be conceived and delivered. A man too may also have a similar experience. The procedure for deliverance is the same. Another step is to ensure you do nothing that amounts to cooperation with the devil. In other words, live a holy life. Beloved, no matter our level of success now, we all need a new beginning. May the merciful God grant us a new beginning as we cooperate with Him in Jesus name. Shalom! The post Deliverance is key to a new beginning, by Funmi Komolafe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GENERAL BABANGIDA AT 85: Another tribute, by Dele Sobowale
items.description: ”Nobody is worth being called a friend unless he is prepared to suffer attacks on account of defending you” – Anonymous Annual tributes to former military President Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida, IBB, has become a ritual; shared by several highly respected individuals than most people realize. Despite the determined efforts by the June 12 opportunists, all they can actually point to is the fact that the June 12, 1993 election was annulled. As is always the case with propagandists, they conveniently ignore the fact that if the first primaries, which produced Adamu Ciroma for the NRC and Shehu Yar’Adua of the SDP, had not been annulled by IBB, Abiola would never have been a candidate at all. Obviously, as far as the hypocrites are concerned, it was acceptable to cancel a primary which ended with two northerners emerging as the candidates!!! In fact, they endorsed the measure by IBB. “A man who has made no mistakes does not usually make anything” – Edward Phelps, VBQ p 141 Only God is infallible. All humans are prone to error; sometimes under external pressure. Granted, a serious mistake was made when the June 12, 1993 election was annulled, nobody can claim to know how things would have worked out if Abiola was president. I had my fears. Any country which unites the greatest personal wealth with the ultimate political power in one person has already murdered democracy. That was what an Abiola presidency could have unleashed. At any rate, we have since then experienced life under six Heads of State, two military and four civilian. Though the circumstances under which each one governed are not the same, one measure of good governance is the establishment and maintenance of institutions. To simplify the comparison, I have chosen to compare Babangida’s eight years in office with those of two elected presidents since 1999 – Obasanjo and Buhari – who both served eight years in office. Despite being very selective in the presentation of evidence, the facts speak for themselves. SELECTED BABANGIDA DECREES AND INSTITUTIONS ESTABLISHED OR STRENGTHENED “A better educated and hopefully more enlightened Nigerian populace will in the future look at these initiatives and wonder: “Where are the monuments to honour the individual who made them possible?” IBRAHIM B BABANGIDA, 1985-1992: LETTING A THOUSAND FLOWERS BLOOM, p 352– Dele Sobowale Babangida did not start the Lagos Third Mainland Bridge. Civilian President Shehu was the initiator. But he had completed less than 25 per cent before his government was overthrown in 1983. Military Head of State, Muhammadu Buhari, ever unimaginative, ignored the uncompleted project during his 19 months in office. IBB came to power and immediately saw the potentials for the rapid development of Lagos State once the bridge was completed. But, unlike other self-seeking presidents, he did not name the bridge after himself; when he could have done it without a single dissenting voice. Close the bridge for six weeks and experience the difference between excellent statecraft and empty slogans about reforms which impoverish the masses. IBB enriched Lagos and indeed the entire nation immeasurably with that bridge. Nothing else that any president or governor has done can compare. Fortunately, he did more than that. Here are just a few, listed in chronological order – just in order to remind us of the debt of gratitude most of us refuse to express. Count me out. I have lived long enough, traveled to some many countries, worked with so many types of people and read so many publications to know that some people are so incorrigibly biased they would not let facts stand in the way of their prejudices. This is strictly for those with minds still open. 1988: • Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation, NDIC, Decree 25 •Securities and Exchange Commission, SEC, Decree 29 • Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC, Decree 45 1989 •National Economic Reconstruction Fund, NERFUND, Decree 2 •National Population Commission, NPC, Decree 23 •National Directorate of Employment, NDE, Decree 24 •National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, Decree 48 •Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission, RMAFC, Decree 49 1990 •Company and Allied Matters Act, CAMA, Decree 20 • National Council of States, NCS, Decree 27 •Nigeria LNG (Fiscal Incentives, Guarantees and Assurances), Decree 39 1991 •Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Decree 24 • Bank and Other Financial Institutions, BOFI, Decree 25 •Nigeria Export Processing Zone, NEPZ, Decree 34 •Nigeria Export-Import Bank, NEXIM, Decree 38 1992: •Oil Mineral Producing Areas Development Commission. OMPADEC, Decree 23 (now NDDC) • National Institute for Sports, NIS, Decree 31 •National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Degree 38 •National Commission for Women, Decree 42 •Federal Universities of Agriculture, Decree 48 •Consumer Protection Council, Decree 66 • National Communications Commission, NCC, Decree 75 •Chartered Institute of Taxation, Decree 76 •Environmental Impact Assessment, Decree 86 • Pharmaceutical Council of Nigeria, PCN, Decree 91 There were over 300 decrees with which Nigeria is being governed right now. In fact, if all the decrees passed by Babangida were to be repealed, Nigeria would come to a halt. Greatness cannot be better defined. VAT: THE CROWN JEWEL OF UNEQUALLED GOVERNANCE “It is the part of a king to do good to his subjects and be maligned for it” – Alexander the Great, 356-323 BC. Alexander was the mightiest warrior and ruler long before Jesus and Mohammed (PBTW) walked the earth. He experienced, first hand, the irony of a ruler taking measures to develop his nation and improve the social welfare of his subjects. History tells us that he was poisoned by unknown aides. IBB, also a warrior, introduced the Value Added Tax, VAT, by Decree 102 in 1993; operations started in 1994. Dr Kalu Idika Kalu, K-I-K, a Minister, was the brain behind it. K-I-K, a former World Bank Country Manager and Adviser to South Korea, when it was not anywhere near a top 20 economy, wanted Nigeria to benefit from this eminently powerful fiscal policy measure. IBB bought the idea. I was their media ally in a venture which became very painful. Progressives, June 12 apostles, socialists and millions of know-nothings joined in condemning it. IBB stood firm. The federal, states and local governments shared N6.72 trillion in 2024 and N8.61 trillion in 2025, alone in VAT revenue. Today, the major beneficiaries of VAT, APC and NADECO, constituted the strongest opponents of VAT. But, they are neither honest enough to acknowledge they were wrong; nor, honourable enough to express gratitude to the men who made it possible. Where are the monuments erected to honour both IBB and K-I-K for enriching current office holders, who, despite unprecedented revenue, have been increasingly impoverishing Nigerians? Happy birthday Sir. I will never stop appreciating what you have done for Nigeria. GCUOBA LAGOS BRANCH CALLING ALL MEMBERS Sail on Ancient Mariners. The 18th ANCIENT MARINERS SAY CELEBRATION 2026 is scheduled to hold on the first Sunday in September. Among the matters on the day’s agenda are: •INDUCTION CEREMONY OF THE ANCIENT MARINERS OF GCU CLASS SET OF 1972. •LECTURE ON AGEISM: THE PROBLEMS AND PROSPECTS OF SENIOR CITIZENS • FUND RAISING DATE: Sunday September 6, 2026 VENUE: GCUOBA SECRETARIAT, 22 MCNEIL STREET, SABO, YABA TIME: 1.30PM PROMPT Although not an old boy, I am extremely privileged to serve this great school in any way. GCU has produced thousands of eminent Nigerians who have contributed a great deal to the development of Nigeria; one of them made it possible for you to read me today. •Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola The post GENERAL BABANGIDA AT 85: Another tribute, by Dele Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘No no-go areas’ across Balochistan, says Home Minister Langove
items.description: QUETTA: Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove has said there were no “no-go areas” in the province, though terrorists remained active along the Quetta-Karachi national highway and security forces were conducting operations against them. Speaking at a press conference here on Saturday, Mr Langove accused armed groups of carrying out terrorism and extortion in the name of an “independence struggle” and urged people to support the state and national institutions in the fight against terrorism. Mr Langove thanked the people of Balochistan for celebrating Independence Day with enthusiasm and praised the security forces for maintaining security across the province. He highlighted healthcare facilities provided in Kalat and Khaliqabad, saying residents, particularly women, had previously faced difficulties transporting patients to hospitals because ambulances were unavailable. The government had provided 30 to 35 ambulances in the two areas, he said, but alleged that terrorists had taken them away. Minister says terrorists use violence as a cover for extortion, intimidation at the directive of external forces According to Mr Langove, women had appealed to the terrorists in the name of the Quran not to take the ambulances, but their pleas were ignored. He said the groups were not fighting for independence or people’s rights but were depriving local communities of basic facilities and trying to impose their narrative on young people and women. The minister said that terrorist groups were backed by India and Afghanistan and that their leaders were controlled by external forces. He also accused terrorists of collecting extortion money from local landowners. He urged the Baloch people to consider the future of their children and stay away from violence while cooperating with the government and state institutions. Responding to a question, Mr Langove acknowledged the presence of terrorists along the Quetta-Karachi RCD National Highway. He said government action against terrorists was sometimes criticised by political and public circles and urged them to support the state in dealing with the security situation. The minister also disclosed that his convoy came under attack while he was returning from Kalat after attending Independence Day events. He said he was travelling in an SSP vehicle when terrorists attempted to target his vehicle. One of the vehicles in the convoy came under fire during an exchange of gunfire. Police, the Anti-Terrorism Force and Frontier Corps personnel accompanying him confronted the attackers. Six security personnel were injured, he said. They were evacuated and taken to Shaheed Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Raisani Hospital before being shifted to the Trauma Centre in Quetta after receiving initial treatment. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan embassy unveils Qu­aid’s statue in Washington
items.description: AMBASSADOR Rizwan Saeed Sheikh inaugurates the Qu­aid’s statue.—Courtesy Pakistan Embassy in Washington WASHINGTON: A statue of Qu­aid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah was unveiled at the Pakistan Embassy in Washington on Friday, giving the country’s Independence Day celebrations a distinctly historical dimension and placing the founder of Pakis­tan at the centre of a ceremony that also highlighted the evolving Pakistan-United States relationship. Ambassador of Pakistan to the US Rizwan Saeed Sheikh unvei­led the statue during an Indepen­dence Day ceremony attended by members of the Pakistani-American community, diplomats and media representatives. The statue, donated by the Quaid-i-Azam Foundation of Houston, will remain permanently at the embassy. Its unveiling comes as Pakistan prepares to mark Jinnah’s 150th birth anniversary later this year. Paying tribute to the founder, Ambassador Sheikh said the nati­­on remained grateful to Mr Jin­nah for his constitutional struggle and tireless efforts that turned the idea of Pakistan into a reality. “The inspiring leadership of Quaid-i-Azam united the Muslims of the subcontinent under one flag and blessed us with freedom,” he said, urging Pakistanis, particularly those living abroad, to uphold Jinnah’s principles of “Unity, Faith and Discipline”. The Independence Day ceremony began with the hoisting of the national flag to the strains of the national anthem, followed by the recitation of verses from the Holy Quran and the reading of messages from Pakistan’s president, prime minister and deputy prime minister. In his address, Ambassador Sheikh used the occasion to underline Pakistan’s continuing importance to the US and the wider world. His remarks echoed a message issued by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Pakistan’s Independence Day, in which he specifically referred to the two countries’ cooperation on regional mediation, along with critical minerals, energy, counterterrorism, cultural heritage, and trade and investment. The reference to regional mediation is particularly significant given Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts involving Washington and Tehran. Islamabad has sought to use its relations with both sides to facilitate dialogue and help ease tensions between the United States and Iran. The ceremony also included an investiture ceremony for Waqar Ali Khan, who received the President’s Award for Pride of Performance in recognition of his decades of service as a community leader and cultural ambassador in the US. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: FPCCI demands rollback of high taxes on hybrid cars
items.description: HYDERABAD: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) has expressed concern over the sales tax hike on hybrid vehicles, from 8.5 per cent to 25pc, and warned that this short-sighted policy would hurt consumers and cripple the auto industry. In a statement issued on Saturday, Adeel Siddiqui, a member of the FPCCI Executive Committee, noted that tax concessions on hybrid vehicles expired on June 30 and with no new auto policy notified in time, the Federal Board of Revenue restored the general sales tax rate of 25pc on hybrid electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid vehicles. He said that this represented a massive increase from earlier preferential rates of 8.5pc for hybrids up to 1800cc and 12.75pc for those above 1800cc. So, he said, the auto industry was in chaos and automakers have temporarily halted production and stopped issuing invoices because they do not know which sales tax rate to apply. Calls for notifying new auto policy immediately He said that a production halt affected thousands of workers, vendors, and transporters, as well as factory workers, who were losing work and wages due to this policy vacuum. He stated that Pakistan’s energy security was at risk, as it imports about 80pc of its petroleum products, making transport electrification a matter of national security. He said that the government was discouraging fuel-efficient vehicles and keeping the country dependent on expensive imported fuel by making hybrids more expensive. Secondly, he said, investor confidence was eroding, and policy uncertainty was damaging it in new-energy vehicle projects. He said that policy remained regressive, wondering why the government was increasing taxes on hybrids — which offer lower running costs and reduced fuel consumption — while reportedly considering tax relief on vehicles priced above Rs10m. He said that this sends a confusing signal about the government’s policy priorities. He called for an immediate rollback of 25pc sales tax on hybrid vehicles, or at least a reduction to 18pc until the new auto policy was finalised. He demanded that Auto Policy 2026-31 should be notified without delay to provide clarity and stability to the industry. He stressed the need for a phased transition to clean energy with incentives tied to local manufacturing and technology transfer. He said that current policy was a self-inflicted wound that would slow Pakistan’s transition to fuel-efficient vehicles, increase fuel import costs, and damage the auto industry at a time when it was showing signs of recovery. He said that it was high time to act before damage was done to Pakistan’s automotive sector and energy security. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: Captors fed us with garri without water, Eda Oniyo worshippers relive horror in kidnappers’ den
items.description: •Say they trekked about 200 km from Ekiti to Kogi •‘Gang leader lived like a king’ By Adetutu Oyebanjo After more than two months in captivity, 14 worshippers of the Christ Apostolic Church, CAC, Eda Oniyo, Ekiti State, have regained their freedom after N25.5 million ransom was said to have been paid. On April 28, the worshippers were attending an open-air revival in Eda Oniyo, Ilejemeje Local Government Area, when gunmen invaded the service. The officiating pastor was shot and killed during the attack, while 15 worshippers, including women and children, were abducted and taken into the forest. An 82-year-old female captive later died in captivity due to the harsh conditions. Following their release, the 14 survivors were taken to the Ekiti State University Teaching Hospital, EKSUTH, Ado-Ekiti, for medical evaluation and trauma rehabilitation. They remained at the facility for more than a month before they were discharged on Wednesday, August 5. Ordeal Narrating their ordeal after their discharge, some of the victims said they were kept in an uncompleted building and fed once a day with raw cassava. According to them, they were occasionally given garri without water and only had the opportunity to drink water when it rained. They also said they trekked about 200 kilometres from Eda-Oniyo to a location in Kogi State, where they were eventually held for more than 60 days. Several residents of the community have since fled their homes, particularly those living on the outskirts, for fear that the kidnappers could return. The victims also revealed that other people abducted from different parts of the country were being held at the camp. According to them, the leader of the kidnappers lived comfortably in the bush, almost like a king, with communication gadgets and a generator that provided electricity round the clock in the camp. Discharge The process for their discharge began last Tuesday when Governor Biodun Oyebanji received a delegation from Eda-Oniyo led by the monarch, Oba Julius Awolola, who thanked the governor for providing medical care for the victims at the expense of the state government. It was a joyous occasion for the victims, who were visibly excited to leave the hospital after more than a month of treatment. Observers noted that they appeared healthier and better nourished than when they were initially rescued from captivity. The state government provided the victims with uniformed Adire attire and an 18-passenger bus to convey them back to Eda-Oniyo. They were escorted by a security van from the state Rapid Response Squad. The President of the Eda-Oniyo Progressive Union, Dr Rufus Ajayi, received them on behalf of the community. The convoy left EKSUTH and arrived in the community about an hour later, where it was welcomed by a large and jubilant crowd. The community chapter of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, held a thanksgiving service in front of the monarch’s palace after the victims were received. The occasion was also used to observe a minute’s silence in honour of one of the abductees, 82-year-old Mrs Olomi Ogundele, who died in captivity. After the celebrations, the monarch, through the President of the Eda-Oniyo Progressive Union, Dr Ajayi, appealed for the speedy completion of the divisional police station under construction in the community. He also called for the establishment of a military post at the border between Eda-Oniyo and Obbo Aiyegunle in Kwara State to address recurrent clashes between the two communities. Military base Responding to the requests, Governor Oyebanji said the state government remained committed to protecting residents and urged the community to cooperate with security agencies. He said: “This government is here to protect and serve you, and the only way we can serve you better is through your cooperation. “I have listened to your request. The construction of the police station is ongoing, and I will ensure its speedy completion. “Then, Gen. Ogundana, Special Adviser on Security, this is important. I want a military base at Eda-Oniyo. It is extremely important. Whatever it is going to cost us, bring it to me; I will approve it.” The state government also promised to assist the children of the deceased in areas of their interest. The victims thereafter reunited with their families. Initial uproar The release of the captives came after weeks of public outcry and calls for their rescue. About a month before their release, the House of Representatives called for the immediate rescue of the abducted worshippers. The lawmakers urged security agencies to launch coordinated operations to apprehend the perpetrators and prevent a recurrence of the incident. The resolution followed the consideration of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the member representing Ekiti North Federal Constituency, Kolawole Akinlayo, during plenary. Presenting the motion, Akinlayo told the House that the attackers, who were armed with sophisticated weapons and operated in large numbers, “killed a pastor and abducted several congregants, including women, elderly persons and children.” He added: “The gunmen carried out the operation for several minutes without resistance before retreating into nearby forests with their victims.” Akinlayo expressed concern that the incident was a testament to the growing insecurity confronting rural communities and places of worship across the country. He noted that the attack not only resulted in the loss of innocent lives but also violated citizens’ constitutional right to freedom of worship and further eroded public confidence in the country’s security architecture. items.title: Work on $2.5bn ML-1 to begin in January
items.description: Officials from a mission of five multilateral international lenders survey the Karachi Railway Division, as it will be connected to ML-1.—Courtesy Railways • Phase-I covers 480km Karachi-Rohri railway section • Online market engagement with contractors, consultants set for Sept 8 • Project expected to take up to three years to complete LAHORE: Civil work on the $2.5 billion first phase of the Main Line-1 (ML-1) railway project is likely to begin in January 2027, as Pakistan Railways (PR) accelerates market consultations, pre-bid preparations and other processes required to meet the timeline set by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. PR has announced an online early market engagement session for Sept 8, inviting local and international civil works contractors as well as project design and monitoring consultants to discuss project readiness, procurement progress and strategy, developments since March and other matters related to the first phase. “We are trying our level best to launch this project as early as possible. The prime minister wants its commencement by January next year by all means,” Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi told Dawn on Saturday. He said early market engagement, international tendering, bidding, shortlisting of contractors and consultants and award of contracts could take four to five months, but PR would make every effort to have the project launched by the prime minister in January. The first phase of ML-1 covers the 480km Karachi-Rohri/Sukkur section, where new up and down tracks will be laid along with fencing on both sides to prevent unauthorised access by people, animals and vehicles. The project is expected to take between two-and-a-half and three years to complete and will serve a corridor carrying 76 per cent of passenger and 98pc of freight traffic, besides connecting major population centres and industrial zones. The project is expected to be financed by the Asian Development Bank, while co-financing is being explored from AIIB, EIN, the World Bank and IsDB. Its indicative scope includes civil and track works on the Keamari-Landhi-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Nawabshah and Nawabshah-Rohri sections, including track reconstruction, limited realignments, bridges, culverts and other structures, stations, freight yards and buildings. The plan also includes upgrading Walton Academy, signalling and telecommunications across the corridor, project management and supervision consultancy services. During engagement with contractors and consultants, discussions will cover package sizes and scope, qualification criteria and joint-venture structures, experience requirements, signalling and telecommunications packages, bid preparation periods, technical and financial weightings, risk allocation, construction under live railway operations, local industry participation and climate-resilient and digital solutions. “Karachi-Rohri and Rohri-Multan are the most critical railway sections where most derailments and accidents take place due to the existing decaying track, which is repaired off and on at a huge cost. This is why PR has selected the Karachi-Rohri section as the first to start the ML-1 project,” a PR official told Dawn. The official expressed confidence that work could begin in January, or possibly earlier, given the government’s priority attached to the project. He said the upgraded infrastructure would enable trains to operate at speeds of up to 160km per hour. Meanwhile, an important meeting on the ML-1 project was held at PR headquarters on Saturday, chaired by Railway Board Chairman Syed Mazhar Ali Shah and attended by international design and review consultants and senior railway officials. The meeting reviewed the planned upgrade of the Karachi-Rohri section, project preparations, progress and the future course of action. Mr Shah directed that the review phase of the ML-1 project be completed by Oct 30, 2026, and ordered weekly monitoring of progress. It was also decided that the second phase of market consultations would begin on Sept 8, involving detailed discussions with market experts and relevant stakeholders on project preparation, technical issues and the way forward. PR said international experience, market proposals and expert opinions would be used to make the project more effective, modern and viable, while merit, transparency and competitiveness would be ensured throughout preparation and implementation. Mr Abbasi expressed satisfaction over the progress, describing ML-1 as the foundation for the development and modernisation of Pakistan Railways and its future requirements. “The upgradation of the project will significantly improve train speeds, passenger facilities and the overall performance of Pakistan Railways,” he said in a statement. He said the project would be further strengthened in light of expert recommendations and stressed that there would be no compromise on merit, transparency and competitiveness. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: Avalanche risk, bad weather disrupt climbing season in Gilgit-Baltistan
items.description: GILGIT: Climate change-induced shifts in weather patterns have worsened conditions on the peaks of the Karakoram Range in Gilgit-Baltistan, creating serious difficulties for mountaineers. No climber managed to summit the world’s second-highest mountain, K2 (8,611 metres), or Gasherbrum-I (8,080 metres), this summer. Around 40 foreign climbers also failed to reach the summits of Gasherbrum-II (8,035 metres), Broad Peak (8,047 metres) and Nanga Parbat (8,126 metres) this year. Persistent storms, heavy snowfall, unstable snow conditions and an exceptionally high avalanche risk created hurdles for climbers attempting to summit peaks in Gilgit-Baltistan, particularly five of the 14 eight-thousanders. No climber managed to summit K2, Gasherbrum-I this summer Expedition teams usually spend weeks at base camps assessing weather forecasts, fixing ropes and acclimatising before beginning their summit push. Mountaineers have experienced persistent bad weather, avalanches, rockfalls, strong winds and unpredictable conditions at the peaks during the summer season for the past two years. The climbing season on the Karakoram peaks, including K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum-I and Gasherbrum-II, usually runs from the end of July to mid-August. ‘Over 200 attempted’ Ghulam Muhammad, a tour operator, told Dawn that more than 200 climbers attempted to summit K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum-II and Gasherbrum-I this year. “This year, continued bad weather kept teams at base camp, while repeated summit attempts were called off due to unsafe conditions on the mountains.” He said only three foreign expedition groups reached the summit of Gasherbrum-II, while members of one local expedition team successfully summited Broad Peak. Earlier, two expedition teams had summited Nanga Parbat, where the climbing season closes by the end of June. Ayaz Shigri, general secretary of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, told Dawn that weather conditions at the peaks remained unstable this summer. However, he said that after the devastating tragedy at Broad Peak on July 30, in which 10 foreign climbers, including Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, lost their lives when a snow avalanche struck them during their summit attempt, many climbers at K2 and Gasherbrum-I abandoned their missions and joined the search and rescue operation. Asghar Porik, another tour operator, said shifting weather patterns in the mountains had made it difficult for mountaineers to plan their summit attempts. “For 100 or 500 years, climbers have planned their attempts in the Karakoram according to established weather patterns. They usually attempt K2 between July 20 and August 15, with the weather generally considered suitable until the end of June,” he said. He said the situation had worsened in recent years as rising temperatures made snow unstable and increased the risks of avalanches and rockfalls. Asghar Porik added that his 11-member expedition team at Gasherbrum-II could not find a suitable weather window and called off its expedition. Ikram Baig, president of the GB Association of Tour Operators, said Broad Peak was considered one of the comparatively less dangerous eight-thousanders. “Broad Peak is often described by experienced mountaineers as one of the comparatively less technical 8,000-metre peaks. However, fresh snowfall can make even an easier route extremely dangerous by creating unstable snow conditions and a high risk of avalanches,” he said. Mr Baig said climate change had altered conditions and made the environment at the peaks increasingly uncertain. Mohammad Ali Nagari, a tour operator, said the growing number of commercial expeditions was also degrading the fragile environment at the peaks. Ayaz Shigri said the summer climbing season on the Karakoram peaks had now closed, with climbers returning from the eight-thousanders without summiting K2 or Gasherbrum-I this year. Last year, too, foreign climbers faced similar conditions and mostly returned without summiting peaks in GB. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: Health Ministry reviews NDC manifesto commitments
items.description: The Ministry of Health has begun a three-day mid-year review of the government’s health sector commitments under the NDC 2024 Manifesto, with a focus on progress, implementation challenges and measures to accelerate delivery. The review, which began in Ho on Saturday, August 15, 2026, brings together heads of agencies, institutions and programmes under the Ministry, led by the Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh. The meeting is expected to provide a comprehensive assessment of progress on key government commitments aimed at improving access to quality, affordable and equitable healthcare. Among the initiatives under review are the Free Primary Healthcare programme, the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (MahamaCare), the expansion of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), the retooling of health facilities and the introduction of specialised nursing programmes. The Ministry said heads of the various agencies and programmes would present updates on their respective areas, outlining achievements, challenges and measures needed to speed up implementation. The review will also assess progress on the construction of additional regional hospitals in the six newly created regions and the establishment of cataract centres in selected regions. Other areas include the formalisation of allowances for nursing trainees, recruitment of health professionals and the completion of abandoned health projects. The Ministry said the discussions were intended to identify implementation gaps and agree on practical measures to ensure that the government’s health sector commitments translated into improved services for Ghanaians. Participants include board chairpersons and chief executives of health agencies, as well as directors of the Ministry. As part of the retreat, participants will undergo training in Public Financial Management to strengthen financial discipline, accountability and the efficient use of public resources within the health sector. Opening the meeting, Mr Akandoh highlighted some achievements recorded in the sector and commended the various agencies whose work had contributed to those outcomes. He, however, charged board chairpersons and heads of agencies to ensure strict compliance with the Public Financial Management Act , stressing the need for prudent and efficient management of public funds. The Minister said responsible financial management was essential to ensuring that resources allocated to the health sector were used effectively to achieve intended outcomes. Universal health coverage The Ministry said the review formed part of its broader efforts to monitor implementation of the government’s health agenda and strengthen coordination among its agencies and programmes. items.title: Les débarquements de pêche à Tanger en hausse de 98%
items.description: Les débarquements de la pêche côtière et artisanale au niveau du port de Tanger ont atteint 5.239 tonnes (T) à fin juillet 2026, en hausse de 98% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente, selon l'Office national des pêches (ONP). La valeur marchande de ces captures a progressé de 14% à 146,15 millions de dirhams (MDH) à fin juillet dernier, contre plus de 128,70 MDH à fin juillet 2025, a précisé l'ONP dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques de la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont progressé de 111% au cours des sept premiers mois de cette année à 3.630 T, pour une valeur estimée à 74,39 MDH (+18%), contre environ 62,97 DH/1.722 T à fin juillet 2025. Les débarquements des poissons blancs se sont, quant à eux, accrus de 125% à 999 T, pour une valeur de plus de 35,17 MDH (+35%), contre environ 25,99 MDH/ 444 T une année auparavant. S'agissant des débarquements des céphalopodes, ils ont augmenté de 32% à 440 T pour des recettes de plus de 27,42 MDH (-7%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont augmenté de 11% à 169 T, générant des revenus de plus de 9,16 MDH (-12%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à 551.547 T à fin juillet dernier, en hausse de 5% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 2% à plus de 6,28 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre 6,15 MMDH en glissement annuel. items.title: South Korean president proposes talks with North to formally end war
items.description: SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea on Saturday to formally end the long-running Korean war, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Moscow while asserting its status as an “irreversible” nuclear state. The two Koreas remain technically at war because their 1950-53 conflict ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty. Lee made the proposal in his speech at a ceremony marking the anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japan’s 1910-45 colonial rule. “Let us put down our intention to threaten each other and begin discussions to end the long-running war as the directly involved parties,” Lee said in his speech. Two countries are still at war since their 1950s confrontation ended without a peace treaty “Through this, it may also be possible to discuss effective measures to halt the advancement of North Korea’s nuclear capabilities,” he added. Lee’s proposal came as North Korea this week denounced upcoming annual US-South Korean military drills, warning of stronger deterrence measures. Pyongyang has also recently been bristling over Tokyo’s gradual military build-up in the Pacific, firing off two missiles in as many weeks after the latter pledged to up its defence capabilities with a “sense of urgency and crisis”. North Korea has repeatedly declared itself an “irreversible” nuclear state since a 2019 summit between Kim and US counterpart Donald Trump in Hanoi collapsed over the scope of denuclearisation and sanctions relief. South Korea’s dovish President Lee has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor since taking power in June last year, offering the nuclear-armed North talks without preconditions. Last month, South Korea’s unification minister even claimed Seoul had abandoned its campaign prioritising pressure on the North to dismantle its nuclear weapons, focusing instead on halting the expansion of Pyongyang’s nuclear activities. The hermetic leadership of North Korea has yet to respond to Lee’s repeated offers, and has instead bolstered military ties with Russia. Analysts say Pyongyang is receiving financial support, food, energy and military technology from Moscow for supplying troops and munitions for Russia’s war in Ukraine. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is expected to visit Russia later this year, potentially to discuss further weapons supplies to Moscow. Washington, Seoul’s key security ally, stations about 28,500 troops in South Korea to bolster the country’s defences against military threats from Pyongyang. Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US and South Korean combined forces command, said this week that North Korea’s deployment to the European war had changed the threat his soldiers may face on the Korean peninsula. “They’ve taken those lessons they learned there and brought them back to North Korea,” he told reporters as he talked about the 11-day South Korea-US joint exercises due to begin on Monday. “Our training accounts for that threat.” Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: Forces eliminate 10 terrorists in Khuzdar operation
items.description: • Several others injured as three hideouts targeted in Shor Pard • Search underway for those who escaped QUETTA: Security forces killed 10 terrorists and injured many others in an intelligence-based operation in Shor Pard area of Khuzdar district on Saturday. During the operation, security forces cordoned off and engaged multiple terrorist hideouts. Accor­ding to security sources, the terrorists were operating in three separate groups, leading to an intense exchange of fire with the security forces. “As a result of the operation, 10 terrorists were killed, while several others sustained injuries,” security sources said. They said that following the engagement, security forces launched an extensive search and clearance operation across the surrounding area. Efforts were underway to track down the terrorists who managed to escape. Security forces have reaffirmed their determination to continue targeted operations against terrorist elements and to eliminate the threat of terrorism from the region. They pledged that the search operation would continue until all remaining terrorists were located and brought to justice. Tribute paid to forces Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to security forces for the successful operation in the mountainous region of Shor Parod, state-run APP reported. “Security forces killed 10 terrorists in a successful operation. Successful operations against terrorists who are enemies of humanity, are a manifestation of the expertise of our security forces,” he said in a statement. “The entire nation is with the security forces in the war against terrorism. We are determined to completely eradicate terrorism from the country,” he added. The development came a day after Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove survived an armed attack on his convoy while returning to Quetta after attending a flag-hoisting ceremony in Kalat. Armed men hiding in the mountains targeted the convoy in the Kund Umrani area of Khad Kocha as it travelled along the Quetta-Karachi National Highway, injuring nine people, including seven police personnel deployed to protect the minister. On Wednesday, the military’s media wing said eight terrorists were killed when explosive material detonated during the preparation of a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device in the Surab district of Balochistan. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, security forces launched a comprehensive clearance operation following the explosion on Monday morning, tracking down and killing another 10 terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan. The initial explosion of explosive material also resulted in civilian casualties and ISPR said that at least three civilians lost their lives in a secondary detonation of other explosives stored at the terrorists’ hideout. “In total, 18 terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan have been eliminated so far,” the ISPR said, adding that two soldiers were injured during an exchange of fire. Published in Dawn, August 16th, 2026

items.title: Qatar denies claims of detaining Iranian pilots
items.description: Qatar on Saturday denied claims that it had detained Iranian pilots, describing them as misleading amid ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating regional tensions. "We categorically deny the claims circulating regarding the detention of Iranian pilots and are surprised by these misleading statements at this particular time," Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said in a post on social media platform X. Al Ansari said contact had been established with the pilots concerned after they violated Qatari airspace and authorities confirmed the trajectory of the targeting. The spokesperson said search and rescue teams later found the remains of ‌one of the pilots and that it had contacted Iran to coordinate a handover. An Iranian military commander said earlier that Qatari forces captured three Iranian pilots whose fighter jets were shot down when returning from a military mission against a US base in Qatar in March. The commander noted that one of the four Iranian pilots in the jets died and that the rest were captured alive by Qatari forces. The Iranian pilots were not allowed to contact their families, and the relevant authorities were also prevented from following up on their cases, he said. The body of the slain Iranian pilot, Majid Kazemi, was returned to Iran and buried in the southern city of Shiraz in late July. Strait of Hormuz shipping deadlock continues Progress toward peace talks and oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz remained stalled, with no sign the warring parties were moving toward ending the conflict. Trump said on Friday that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory after "defeating Iran," according to remarks made at a political rally. "This strait will be opened and closed only under Iran's command, and so long as you do not accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in fantasies, Iran will continue to enforce the blockade," Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X. Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that talks between Iran and Oman are still making active progress, with the two sides having reached an agreement on arrangements for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran had not decided to resume talks with the US, he said, adding that Washington must meet conditions on the strait for shipping to resume in the waterway. Israel-Lebanon conflict intensifies Hezbollah on Saturday called on the Lebanese authorities to stop pursuing direct negotiations with Israel, describing the talks as "humiliating." In a statement following Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon earlier in the day, the group accused Israel of continuing a campaign of attacks against Lebanese civilians, homes and agricultural areas. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said in a statement on the same day that it killed a commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force during overnight strikes in southern Lebanon. The IDF said the militant was identified as Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a battalion commander in the unit. It added that he was struck in Hezbollah's headquarters in the town of Ansar, Nabatieh District, in response to an attack on Israeli forces operating in the "security zone." At least 11 people were killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon on Saturday, the Lebanese ‌health ministry said. The strikes were some of the deadliest in the weeks since the country agreed to a US-mediated peace framework with Israel. (With input from agencies)

items.title: Lagos overwhelmed by 15,000 tons of waste everyday —Gbadegesin, LAWMA boss
items.description: •Says Alimosho, Amuwo-Odofin, Ojo, Ikorodu worst hit •‘10,000 people living on Badagry road median, setback alone, messing up the environment’ By Olasunkanmi Akoni Amid the current waste crisis across Lagos metropolis with the attendant health risks, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, in this exclusive interview, speaks on refuse heaps, infrastructure gaps, new waste management system, enforcement and the way forward for Lagos among others. Lagos has been facing infrastructure deficit in waste management in recent times. What are the challenges and interventions being deployed? Lagos is a rapidly growing megacity of about 22 million people. We generate between 13,000 to 15,000 tons of waste daily. To manage that, you need significant investment across the entire value chain of waste management which starts with containerization of waste, which, of course, is the trash bins or waste bins, which are used to keep waste in each household or business before collection. Once you containerize the waste, that waste has to be collected regularly, and for that you need trucks, and in Lagos, we use compactor trucks to do house-to-house collection. We are expecting by the end of this year Transfer Loading Stations, TLS, should be completed. Then, the MRFs, sometime in the first quarter of next year. At that point, we can close down Olusosun. One is already closed. ln the area of treatment and disposal, we have a long-term project, five-year project to build a biogas plant. That is a partnership between LAWMA and Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority, LAMATA. We completed the feasibility study about a year ago, funded by the government of Sweden. And, I’m sure you’re aware that Sweden has achieved a very high level of circularity. We have been partnering with their government to replicate some of the achievements. Since 1942, the city of Stockholm has been treating their organic waste, both solid and liquid, and using that to produce biogas, which they pipe to homes for cooking, and heating the houses. They also use it for their public transport fleet. They have a network of filling stations where the buses can fill up with biomethane. Biogas We have started doing that in Lagos with the energy transition. LAMATA is bringing in about 2,000 CNG-powered buses. The plan is that those buses will after we have constructed the biogas plant, be powered by biomethane produced from our organic waste, which is 50 per cent of the waste that we generate daily. In addition, we are also installing, biodigesters at the markets which generate high volume of organic waste. We’ve already started with the Ikosi Fruit Market, that’s a pilot project we launched in February. We want to place similar small-scale biodigesters at other markets like Alamutu, Mile 12, and Afolabi Ege. These are some of the markets that you see in the media with mountains of waste. Like Alamutu, you see huge piles of rotting plantain or plantain stalk. This is a high-quality raw material for production of biofertilizer. There is no point going to bury it in the landfill. We want to place those in all these markets so that they will have treatment of waste. Smart bins We have also made some investment in the area of containerization. The state government has about 80,000 smart bins, which are not free. The adoption rate has been somewhat slow. What we’re looking at right now is a situation where we can distribute it free to households, and then we’ll be adding a small amount to the bill every month so that you pay it off. We want to roll that out by the end of the year as well. By the end of this year, we are expecting 150 new compactor trucks. Each of the 57 local governments and Local Council Development Areas, LCDAs, have ordered two, and the state government is ordering 36, making 150. This will form part of a new unified waste management fleet that we will jointly manage with the local governments. By next year, we’re hoping to do a lot more in terms of new trucks. Our target is to have 2,000 trucks. To support that new system, we are going to do a lot of reform of the PSP programme. I’m not prepared to go into too much detail about that now. PSPs operation When next we discuss, I should be able to shed more light on that. There are already internal planning going on among the state government, Ministry of Environment, the House of Assembly, and the Association of Waste Managers to see how we can redesign the PSP system so that it can be more efficient, effective and responsive to the needs of Lagosians who are, after all, paying for that service. LAWMA is aware that there are a lot of complaints about delayed collection and a lot of dissatisfaction with the waste collection services. We plead with Lagosians for understanding, and also I’d like to take this opportunity also to let Lagosians know that you can reach out to us directly when you have any issue on our free call lines. You can call these lines, you won’t be charged. 070 8060 1020 and 0800 0052 962, and you can also reach out to us on our email: info@lawma.gov.ng . If you send an email, you can attach your payment receipt so that we can look into whatever dispute you might have with the PSP operator or whatever complaint. We also invite those who want to get involved, like I said, it’s public-private partnership. If you have expertise or interest in any of those services that we need to provide to citizens we want to work with private sector players who are credible, who can deliver the services. You can also reach out to us by email, because we believe strongly that we have people out there who have the capacity to help in solving some of the problems. Human challenge On human behavior, this is another big challenge. It is a big city of 22 million people. Not everyone is going to comply. Even in places where you have regular PSP service, there are people who want to evade, they don’t want to pay, and have formed the habit of dumping their waste anywhere they please. That’s a big challenge for us because another thing that makes it even more difficult is that we have people coming into Lagos every day, and not everyone understands the way we manage waste. Most Lagosians, from my observation, are abiding by the rules, but there are a lot of people who are living on the streets. And I see them as climate migrants. They’re coming here for many reasons, including insecurity and natural disasters. They flood into Lagos. They sleep on the streets. In the last two years, I have seen like a doubling of the population of people sleeping on the sidewalks. Some of them are on drugs. That is a major problem now. We continually do advocacy. We go to markets, we go to communities, we work with Community Development Associations, CDAs, and Community Development Committees, CDCs, with the local government, preaching to people that they should follow the laid-down rules and regulations with waste management, but there are still a lot of violations of that process. That’s why we’ve expanded our enforcement operations. 10,000 beggars The most visible in the last couple of months is the major enforcement along the Badagry Expressway, where we did some initial study and we discovered that over 10,000 people after a census were living on that corridor. On the road, the median, the setback, living and carrying out their daily activities, buying, selling, everything, all bodily activities, they were doing right on the road. In fact, the most alarming example was one of them who had sunk a borehole on the median of the expressway and was selling water to the other people around there. We have been there for more than a month now, working with Rapid Response Squad, RRS, the task force, Kick Against Indiscipline, KAI officials, military officers from OP MESA, and we have done a lot. If you go there today, you will still see that we are still out, there is a large military presence there to clear that expressway. The development is moving quite well, the expressway construction and also construction of the Blue Line, which has been a very successful project, is being extended down as well. We want to clear that so that we can have that good infrastructure to serve communities in that area. Clampdown We have done a lot of arrests, and we have done a lot of advocacy. We have shut down some of the markets. We have shut down a lot of markets that are deliberately flouting the regulations. And we will continue to do that. For us, ensuring that there is no waste in public spaces is a matter of health and safety for everyone because waste that is not cleared promptly can lead to disease outbreak, epidemic outbreak. Waste that is not cleared promptly washes back into the drainage, blocks the drainage, and causes flooding. It’s not just flooding, it also leads to destruction of the road infrastructure because if the water is pooled, the road is going to be destroyed, it’s almost like you’re grinding away the asphalt. That’s why we take that seriously, we can’t allow a few people because of their own convenience or economic interest, dump the waste, indiscriminately. Advocacy In the area of advocacy, we’ve also started something new, which is catching them young. The Governor has established the LAWMA Academy. That was his initiative about four years ago, and we’ve kept that going. Last Monday, we opened the summer school. We have an annual summer school, and you see the kids are here learning and doing practical exercises, building things out of waste. We have monthly internship programmes for undergraduates and graduates who come here for four to six weeks, and they learn about circular economy, waste to wealth, and they do a project before they leave. If you followed the news, we shut down a lot of fashion design outlets around Tejuosho, and Yaba over the weekend, for dumping waste and scrap on the roads. We’ve been warning them for a long time, they refused to listen, so we had to seal them. And that’s part of the behavioral modification that is necessary. Why are you throwing away scrap? And that material actually has value, because if you see what they made out of it. I don’t know why they are throwing it away. After they’re going to come here, we’re going to talk to them, we’re going to see how we can collect that textile and use it for other purposes. Partnership Every incident of illegal dumping of waste has a different reason. It’s not one size fits all. And that’s why one of the things we’ve done differently in the last two years, we established a Waste Investigation, Surveillance, and Enforcement Unit whose job is to find those who dumped waste illegally. What we used to do in the past is you clear it. That’s LAWMA’s job. If there’s waste illegally, you just go and clear it. But the next day you come back, you see the same waste, and you clear it again. And what we realized is that the more you clear it and the faster you clear it, the faster they’re going to bring it, because they actually think, okay, that’s where these people want us to be bringing the waste. A lot of people actually believe that this is where LAWMA is going to collect it, Go and put your waste there and they stopped waiting for the PSP operators. Those who were paying stopped paying. The point of the purpose of the Waste Investigation, Surveillance, and Enforcement Unit is to trace where it’s coming from and why it’s coming there. Their job is: once we clear, you’re supposed to mark with caution tape. And you’re now supposed to go and engage with the community around, whether it’s a market or residential, engage with the PSP operator, What’s going on here? Ask the PSP operator, Who are the people complying? Who are the non-compliants? Who is owing,? ” so that we can get to the root of that waste leakage and stop it. LAWMA The role of the local government in that is that we ask each of them to set up a waste management task force. Now, that task force has a representative from LAWMA, the CDA and CDC, the PSP operator, the environmental health officer, and other stakeholders within that community. They are expected to meet on a regular basis, at least once monthly, to resolve issues of waste management within that local government. The local government, in addition, have been buying their own compactor trucks so that they can respond to some of these illegal dump sites as, you know, faster than maybe what LAWMA can do. And in addition, we have started licensing some of the local governments to have their own collection system. What we have discovered is that even before now, the trucks they’re buying are used trucks as well. The new ones, they’re going to be new trucks that I mentioned earlier, the 104 trucks are brand new trucks. We discovered that in a lot of areas in Lagos, a compactor truck cannot even access the community because of bad road, or in a place like Lagos Island, the streets are very narrow. Trucks Two years ago, Ibeju-Lekki chairman came here and told us, “This is the issue. The PSP can’t access most of these communities that he wants to introduce tricycle compactors. And we said, “excellent”, because as part of our study tour, we had gone to Ghana, and we saw how they were using tricycle compactors very effectively. And we went to Ibeju-Lekki, and at the same time, there was a young entrepreneur who had brought in some tricycle compactors. We put them together, gave license to the local government, and they’ve been working together since then. And people are paying. It’s not free. They pay N800 per bin bag. They distribute bin bags. Once it’s full, they come and collect. They pay with POS. And then the local government has a compactor truck that they use to evacuate waste from the tricycle compactor to the dump site. Since then, Lagos Island has joined that system. Lagos Island is making use of our Simpson TLS because the compactor can’t go all the way to the dump site. They come to the TLS and then we assist them to evacuate to the dump site. Badagry has also started, and many of the other local governments are going to introduce that. Another partnership with the local governments is to establish mini-transfer loading stations in each local government that the tricycle compactors, or those communities which need it, or the compactor truck can go and dump in that TLS, and then we can evacuate from that transfer loading station to either it’s TLS or straight to the MRF. That’s another thing that we’re working out with the local governments. We met with them, a business meeting, not political meeting about two months ago, and we’ve given them the design for those mini TLS. What they are doing now is identifying land where we can site those locations. Even the mini transfer loading station is going to be a business opportunity. When we have those locations, we’re going to let people take charge and operate those, because when the tricycle compactor has collected money, so when it comes to that mini TLS, it will just deduct something from the wallet, from their POS, to pay to dump in that. That makes it sustainable. That’s exactly what they’re doing in Ghana. The idea now, what we want to do, is that some of those cart pushers, the ones who have who are manageable, that you can train properly; we can use them to operate the tricycle collection vehicles. Instead of using the cart, they’ll operate the tricycle. We will put them in uniform, they will have ID card, they’ll be regulated, and those are the ones who will be doing all this collection. Then the TLS, maybe the TLS will be operated by somebody who was formerly a PSP operator. He has a truck, you can just park the truck there, come, and they’ll dump, then he’ll collect his own money from them. They’ll go back and collect more. That is what we’re trying to introduce. But in doing that, I am not saying that we have all the answers. We are working with the local governments. Some of them are saying, look, they can operate the TLS themselves. In some areas, we can advertise and say, who has the capacity to operate this, let them come and operate it. But we’ll ensure that everybody gets something out of it, and that’s how it will be manageable. Illegal waste collection You notice there’s a resurgence of waste on Agege Motor Road. We clear that daily. If you pass through there right now, you’ll see four to five trucks clearing. As we’re clearing, they are bringing out huge sacks of waste. Once we clear one section, within one hour, you’ll just see people bringing out, carrying on their head. And we found out that somebody was actually operating a illegal waste collection business. They bought big sacks, they had recruited some boys for collection. LAWMA is clearing this thing. They now go and they charge people to bring out their waste, and they come and just drop it on the road for LAWMA to collect. Meanwhile, they’ve made money on their own, because in most of those areas, there are no PSP. But you can imagine the population and the impact. Mushin, both sides of Agege Motor Road, heavy population. You can imagine how much money these people are making. But they’re dumping it on the major highway for LAWMA to remove. That we’re talking to both local government chairmen, Odi- Olowo and Mushin, that this can’t go on like this. It’s one of two things. If you as a local government, you can coordinate your boys and your people to bring the waste, we will park our trucks. We can mobilize six trucks along that stretch, so we park them at intervals, and we’ll tell you the time that we’ll be available so that they come and dump, for a fee so that we can buy petrol into the trucks. Environment But we don’t want to be clearing from the median, it doesn’t make any sense. You know, but it’s because the people bringing it out are collecting money. They’re so efficient in bringing out that waste, but the system doesn’t allow that. It doesn’t make sense, it’s not sustainable. Because once what happens is that once there’s waste on that median, and you have people going to do video, blaming and attacking the government. That’s where the collective engagement is essential. Very soon, we’re going to start an engagement exercise with all the local governments. That’s LAWMA, with some people from Ministry of Environment as well, having stakeholder meeting with all the local governments to bring these new systems, to explain what we want from them, because if you don’t do that, you are talking theory. And if people don’t see you, they won’t really understand what you’re talking about. You mentioned incorporating local governments into the new waste system. In specific terms, what have you agreed on? Every illegal dump has a different reason. What we have done is set up a Waste Investigation, Surveillance and Enforcement Unit. Instead of just clearing and leaving, we mark the areas, engage the community, the PSP and Community Development Associations, CDAs to find the root cause. With local governments, we’ve asked each one to set up a Waste Management Task Force with LAWMA, CDA/Community Development Committees, CDCs, PSP, and health officers to meet monthly. We have also started licensing LGs to run their own collection. Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos Island and Badagry are already running tricycle collection on pay-as-you-go. Residents pay N800 per bag via POS. The tricycle brings it to a compactor, which takes it to a TLS. Now, with the 150 new trucks coming, two per LGA/LCDA, we’re asking LGs to provide land for mini-TLS. We’ve given them designs. We’ll inspect the sites. The idea is, tricycles collect, dump at mini-TLS, then our big trucks evacuate to the main MRF. That way trucks don’t have to go house-to-house on bad and narrow roads. Everything requires groundwork and funding, but we’re pushing it to the LGs. We’ve already ordered the new trucks. The question is: do you want those two trucks per LGA collecting on the roadside, or stationed at a mini-TLS with tricycles feeding them? Before the trucks arrive, we want the system designed. We have written LGAs to provide locations. We will go out and inspect. The goal is to have the mini-TLS ready before the trucks land. From your record which parts of Lagos are worst hit in terms of refuse buildup? Alimosho, Amuwo-Odofin, Ojo, Ikorodu especially along the Ikorodu stretch, and Lagos Island councils. Generally, fast-growing areas and heavily built-up urban areas. In GRAs and estates with organized payment, there’s less pressure. But in areas with poor road access, tricycle collection makes more sense. Those are our targets. On enforcement, what are current fines for offenders including community service? We have always had community service. But we’re reviewing the law with the House of Assembly for stiffer penalties. However, enforcement only works when the system is functioning. That’s why we sometimes give 48 hours or seven days notice before sealing. Once the new TLS and MRFs are running, anyone who still dumps will have no excuse. Even if PSP hasn’t come, dumping on the road is not an option. Residents can call us on 07080601020 or 08000052962 to report missed pickups. How do you manage PSP operators who default, like not showing up regularly? We do a monthly performance audit of all PSPs statewide. We check: are trucks working.? Are they coming as scheduled? What’s customer feedback? How many times did they dump at the landfill? They get a score. If they fall below, they get a query. After three queries, we can withdraw their license. Last year we withdrew about 27 out of 450. Same this year. That’s why some areas have gaps and we’re working with LG chairmen to provide backup. **Residents also complain about PSP trucks parking indiscriminately and causing traffic. Is there orientation for them? ** Yes, that is one of the things we query them for. Some of the truck drivers park and start sorting waste on the road. That is against the rules. We’ll keep doing advocacy. We’re also doing a Five-year performance audit and residents can give feedback. If you see it, report to our toll-free lines and we’ll act. items.title: Mfantsipim School @ 150 and Creech’s Mfantsipim Diaries: My First Shock
items.description: My first shock when I entered Mfantsipim School in September 1987 was not the discipline. Not the academic pressure. Not even the intimidating architecture that seemed to breathe history. It was the nicknames of members of staff. In the official register, they were respectable men with proper titles and credentials. But in the unofficial student archive, they had already been renamed, reinterpreted, and absorbed into folklore. I arrived armed with institutional expectations: “Mr.” this, “Sir” that, formal address, procedural decorum. Within days, I discovered that the student body operated a parallel registry of identity. Masters were not merely teachers; they were characters in a living oral tradition. We had names like Corrosive, Ostrich, Doboo, Black Sammy, Hope Man, Shakar, and several others. At first, I was scandalised. How could students reduce respected masters to such irreverent labels? The reaction was naive. I soon realised these nicknames were not casual mockery; they were coded language. An internal anthropology of power. “Corrosive,” our Headmaster, was not named for volume. He rarely raised his voice. But his sarcasm was surgical. His words did not explode; they dissolved. Slowly. Efficiently. Corrosively. “Ostrich,” the Assistant Headmaster (Academic), was tall and distinctive in appearance. The boys exaggerated certain features in private commentary, and the name attached itself with speed. It was observational rather than malicious. Mfantsipim boys are ruthless ethnographers of physical detail. Then there was “Doboo,” the Assistant Headmaster (Domestic). His imposing height earned him the label “Double man,” which, through the natural erosion of schoolboy slang, evolved into “Doboo.” Language, like tradition, adapts. “Black Sammy,” the Senior Housemaster at the time, derived his name plainly from his dark complexion. It was adolescent bluntness, unfiltered and unvarnished. “Hope Man” required less invention. “Man” was simply appended to his surname, Hope. It reflected the school’s instinct for masculine amplification. Titles re-engineered in dormitory conversation. And then there was “Shakar”, the school chaplain. His name was borrowed from a popular Indian film protagonist known for firmness and moral clarity. The comparison was deliberate. The chaplain carried himself with disciplined gravity; the cinematic reference captured that energy in a single stroke. “Slippe Man” was a study in unpredictability. Lenient one moment, lethal the next. Like a slipper skidding across a polished corridor, you never quite knew where you stood. Some names were affectionate. Others defensive. A few were pure satire. But all of them functioned as coping mechanisms within the rigid architecture of boarding school life. Founded in 1876 and steeped in Methodist discipline and academic rigour, Mfantsipim School has always demanded much of its boys. Humour became our pressure valve. As adolescents navigating hierarchy, fear, ambition, homesickness, and testosterone, we needed a language that restored balance. The nicknames levelled the field. They reminded us that authority, however formidable, was still human. Nearly four decades later, what strikes me is not the irreverence, but the creativity. We were archivists without knowing it. Each name captured an essence: temperament, physique, speech pattern, hometown, or one unforgettable incident. They were ethnographic shorthand. They also bound us together. To know the nickname was to belong. It signified initiation into the fraternity of shared experience. You were no longer a bewildered Greenhorn; you were a Kwabotwe boy who understood the code. In hindsight, those names were part of the hidden curriculum of Mfantsipim. Beyond Mathematics, Science, and Literature, we learned: • How to interpret power • How to survive scrutiny • How to build solidarity • How to laugh under pressure Institutions endure for 150 years not only because of formal structures, but because of informal cultures that make endurance possible. The nicknames were small acts of authorship in a long institutional narrative. Today, when I hear “Corrosive” or “Ostrich,” I do not hear mockery. I hear adolescence finding its voice. I hear boys rehearsing adulthood. I hear memory compressing complexity into symbol. I entered Mfantsipim as Philip Creech-Jones, officially reformatted as Creech-Jones, P. But among my mates, I became Creech. Dizzy Kay. Santana. And the less flattering Shasha Marley. Perhaps that was my true initiation in September 1987. Not when the school registered my name. But when it renamed me. What was your first shock? The writer is Philip Creech-Jones of MOBA 1992 (Mfantsipim Old Boys Association).
